# Engine theme value sheets outrank consumer theme-root projections: the dock layer's `:where()` weight is the pattern, `tooltip/Base.scss` the first case

## Context

PR #18098 (#18096) found that the Workstation's established projection idiom — `:root .neo-theme-neo-* { --tooltip-bg: var(--workstation-panel-2) }` in `theme-neo-*/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss` — has no effect on the shared tooltip: `theme-neo-*/tooltip/Base.scss` declares the same tokens at the same `:root .neo-theme-neo-*` selector, (0,2,0), and its per-class sheet is appended after the app's, so the tie resolves on load order and the theme wins. The PR routed around it with an element-scoped bridge (`body:has(.workstation-viewport) .neo-tooltip`, (0,2,1)) — correct, and the third such bridge in that app.

**Measured** at `2dcbcf9752` (2026-09-02): 105 of the 108 `theme-neo-dark` sheets open with `:root .neo-theme-neo-dark {`; two open with `:where(.neo-theme-neo-dark) {` — `dashboard/Container.scss` and `dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.scss`, both from #17242 / PR #17293 (the dock values layer). The same split holds in `theme-neo-light`. That `:where()` weight is why the Workstation's `--agent-dock-preview-*` projections at theme-root win cleanly even though the theme declares `--agent-dock-preview-signal-ground` itself.

## The Problem

Two weights, one contract. A consumer that projects its palette into an engine token family at theme-root — the documented path, "a consumer filling engine token slots" — wins against the two `:where()` sheets and ties (then loses on load order) against the other 105. Which case applies is invisible until measured: the symptom reads as "the tokens do not work" (PR #18098's first shape measured byte-identically to the baseline). Each consumer then grows per-element `body:has()` bridges for what the token layer promised to do.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/theme-neo-{dark,light}/**/*.scss` — the value layers: 105 + 105 sheets at (0,2,0), 2 + 2 at (0,0,0).
- `resources/scss/src/**` — the structure sheets read `var(--token)`; untouched by any of this.
- Consumer projections: `theme-neo-*/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss` (`:root .neo-theme-neo-*`); the institution's cockpit sheets carry the same shape.
- CSS: `:where()` contributes zero specificity; `:root .neo-theme-*` is (0,2,0). A component's own `neo-theme-*` class (`component.Base#afterSetTheme`; the shared tooltip's `applySingletonTargetConfig` stamps the hovered target's theme onto itself) means the theme rule matches the element itself, so own-vs-inherited does not rescue a tie.

## The Fix

Make `:where(.neo-theme-neo-*)` the weight of the engine's theme VALUE sheets, so a consumer declaration at (0,2,0) or above wins by specificity regardless of load order — the pattern #17293 already established for the dock layer.

1. **First case, one PR:** `theme-neo-{dark,light}/tooltip/Base.scss` → `:where(.neo-theme-neo-*)`. Witness: a component spec whose host projects `--tooltip-bg` at `:root .neo-theme-neo-dark` and reads the projected value on a rendered `.neo-tooltip` — red at `dev`, green at head. The Workstation's bridge stays as is (still correct, no longer load-bearing); retiring it is a follow-up.
2. **Policy:** one paragraph in the theming guide (`learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/StylingAndTheming.md`, or the #18036 slot) — engine value sheets declare at `:where()` weight, consumers project at theme-root.
3. **The remaining sheets:** a mechanical selector change per sheet, but a sheet's own rules may rely on (0,2,0) beating an equal-weight `src` rule — measure before the sweep; ticket the batches once (1) proves the shape.

## Acceptance Criteria (the first case)

- [ ] AC-1 `theme-neo-{dark,light}/tooltip/Base.scss` declare at `:where(.neo-theme-neo-*)`; every other consumer renders byte-identically (no consumer projects `--tooltip-*` at theme-root today except PR #18098's retired first shape).
- [ ] AC-2 A component witness: a host projecting `--tooltip-bg` at `:root .neo-theme-neo-dark` sees the projected value on a rendered `.neo-tooltip`; red-first against `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3 The guide states the two-weight reality and the single-weight resolution.
- [ ] AC-4 The remaining sheets are ticketed as a measured sweep, not assumed safe.

## Out of Scope

- The Workstation's three `body:has()` bridges (PR #18098 and its two siblings) — correct today; retiring them follows (1).
- Runtime skin-class placement (#17984's contest) — the inheritance axis, not specificity.
